catalysts.title: HBM3e & HBM4 Capacity Sold Out Through CY2026/2027 via NVIDIA Blackwell & AMD MI350 Attach
catalysts.probabilityAnchor: Management confirmed entire calendar 2026 HBM allocation is 100% contracted under binding supply agreements, with over 80% of calendar 2027 capacity already allocated to NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra/Rubin and AMD Instinct platforms.
catalysts.description: Micron's 24GB (8-high) and 36GB (12-high) HBM3e modules provide industry-leading 30% lower power consumption over competitors. High attachment rates across NVIDIA GB200/B200 and AMD MI350 accelerators guarantee structurally elevated memory margins (>50% gross margin) and multi-billion-dollar annual revenue.

evidence.fact: Compute and Networking (CNBU) revenue expanded 85% YoY to $5.45B, driven by high-margin HBM3e volume shipments to top cloud accelerator OEMs.
Micron achieved qualification of its 12-high 36GB HBM3e stack with NVIDIA, entering mass volume delivery ahead of Samsung.

catalysts.title: Surging High-Density Enterprise SSD (D5/QLC) Adoption for AI Inferencing & Data Lakes
catalysts.probabilityAnchor: Storage Business Unit (SBU) revenue surged 82% YoY to $2.40B as AI hyperscalers replace legacy hard disk drive (HDD) storage with Micron 60TB+ D5/QLC enterprise SSDs for high-throughput model checkpointing and RAG pipelines.
catalysts.description: Frontier AI reasoning models require rapid retrieval and continuous state persistence. Micron's monolithic 232-layer and 276-layer QLC NAND delivers substantial power and density advantages, converting commoditized NAND bits into high-margin enterprise storage solutions.

evidence.fact: Enterprise SSD revenue grew over 120% YoY in Q3 FY2026, establishing Micron as the #2 global supplier of high-capacity data center QLC SSDs.

catalysts.title: DRAM Blended ASP Expansion & Structurally Constrained Wafer Fab Capacity
catalysts.probabilityAnchor: HBM manufacturing consumes roughly 3x the clean wafer capacity of standard DDR5 for equivalent gigabits, creating an industry-wide wafer supply deficit and lifting commodity DRAM blended pricing by mid-to-high single digits sequentially.
catalysts.description: Because leading memory makers (Micron, SK Hynix, Samsung) are diverting cleanroom wafer starts from standard PC and server DRAM to HBM3e/HBM4 production lines, conventional DDR5, LPDDR5X, and server RDIMMs face structural shortages, driving strong price realization and operating leverage.

evidence.fact: Micron reported DRAM blended average selling prices (ASPs) increased mid-single digits sequentially in Q3 FY2026, with Q4 guidance implying continued ASP expansion.

catalysts.title: PC & Smartphone On-Device AI Memory Content Increases (16GB-32GB DRAM per Device)
catalysts.probabilityAnchor: Next-generation generative AI smartphones and Copilot+ PCs mandate a minimum baseline of 16GB LPDDR5X (up from 8GB-12GB), with premium tier systems scaling to 24GB-32GB to accommodate local 7B-13B parameter LLM inference.
catalysts.description: Even in an environment of low-single-digit unit device growth, memory content per device is surging by 40-70%. Micron's energy-efficient 1-beta LPDDR5X delivers the high memory bandwidth and power envelope required for edge AI execution.

evidence.fact: Mobile Business Unit (MBU) revenue rose 42% YoY to $2.15B, reflecting rich memory content transitions in flagship AI handset launches.

catalysts.title: Samsung & SK Hynix Competitive HBM Yield Recovery & Packaging Scale Pressure
catalysts.probabilityAnchor: Samsung is heavily investing in next-gen packaging and resolving earlier 12-high HBM3e yield hurdles, while SK Hynix retains incumbent market share dominance with TSMC and NVIDIA.
catalysts.description: If Samsung completes full volume qualification of 12-high HBM3e and rapidly converts 1b DRAM capacity, industry HBM availability could normalize by mid-CY2027, tempering HBM price premiums and constraining Micron's target 25% market share trajectory.

evidence.fact: SK Hynix announced expanded capital investments in its Cheongju M15X fab and advanced MR-MUF packaging lines to protect its tier-1 GPU customer allocations.

catalysts.title: Memory Industry Peak-Cycle CapEx Overbuilding & Fab Expansion Risk
catalysts.probabilityAnchor: Historical memory cycles show that multi-year price expansions inevitably incentivize excessive cleanroom and wafer capacity build-outs across Boise, Syracuse, Pyeongtaek, and Yongin.
catalysts.description: Micron and its peers are committing tens of billions of dollars to greenfield megafabs supported by government CHIPS Act subsidies. If hyperscaler AI infrastructure capex moderates in late FY2027 while new fab shells come online, the industry risks a typical cyclical supply overhang.

evidence.fact: Micron guided FY2026 capital expenditure up to $8.5B-$9.0B, with FY2027 projected to increase further as Boise Fab shell construction advances.
